mainTopic: The פשוט and מקושר documents: the sources for their witnesses, why חכמים made the מקושר, where its עדים sign, and how forgery is prevented.
overview: The amud asks where the Torah hints to the two kinds of שטרות: the plain פשוט and the tied מקושר, and why a פשוט needs two עדים while a מקושר needs three. רבי חנינא, רפרם and רמי בר יחזקאל each bring a different פסוק. Each time the גמרא asks why we shouldn't flip the numbers, and each time it answers that the document with more ties gets more witnesses. Then the גמרא shows from a ברייתא that each of these פסוקים really teaches something else. It concludes that the מקושר is a rabbinic rule and the פסוקים are only an אסמכתא. חכמים made it for hot-tempered כהנים, so that the slow process of a tied גט would give them time to calm down, and they extended it to all שטרות. Next comes a dispute about where the עדים sign on a מקושר. רב חסדא explains that רב הונא means between the ties, on the outside. The גמרא then works through worries about forgery, with ״שריר וקיים״ as the safeguard. Its answer from רבי יוחנן continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The verse hints to two documents and two numbers of witnesses
steps.stepSummary: The words of the פסוק are matched up: 'written in a book' is a פשוט, 'sealed' is a מקושר, 'witness' means two, and 'witnesses' means three. So two עדים go with a פשוט and three go with a מקושר.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Write it in a book' means a plain document. 'And seal it' means a tied document. 'And have witnesses' means two, and 'witnesses' means three. How do these fit together? Two witnesses for a plain document, three for a tied document.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes reading the פסוק word by word. It shows that the פסוק hints to two kinds of documents and two different numbers of witnesses.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word עד on its own already means two witnesses, the usual Torah number. The extra word עדים adds a third. Since the פסוק mentions two documents and two numbers, it pairs them: two for the פשוט and three for the מקושר.

keyTerms.meaning: A plain, ordinary document that is written and signed normally
A tied document: folded, sewn, and signed between the folds
'And seal it.' Here it is read as pointing to the tied document
'And have witnesses bear witness.' Read as hinting to two and to three witnesses
'How so?' Used to resolve two things that seem to clash

phrases.english: this is an ordinary document.
phrases.notes: This goes back to the words 'וכתוב בספר', 'write it in a book', from ירמיהו 32:44, quoted just before this.

phrases.english: "And seal" — this is a tied document.
"And have bear witness" — two,
"witnesses" — three.
phrases.notes: The extra word 'witnesses' adds one more witness on top of the basic two.

phrases.english: How so?
Two for an ordinary document,
three for a tied document.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the derivation from ירמיהו 32:44 that started before this part of the daf.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A פשוט needs two עדים and a מקושר needs three, based on the פסוק in ירמיהו.

steps.title: Why not reverse the numbers?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the pairing: maybe the פשוט needs three witnesses and the מקושר needs two.
steps.simpleTranslation: But I could reverse it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the pairing. It asks why the plain document gets two witnesses and the tied one gets three, and not the other way around.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק mentions two documents and two numbers, but it never says which number belongs to which document. So the matching in step 1 still needs a reason.

keyTerms.meaning: 'But I can reverse it.' A challenge that suggests the opposite pairing

phrases.english: But I could reverse it!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the pairing of numbers made in step 1.
steps.kashyaTarget: The assignment of two witnesses to a פשוט and three to a מקושר.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק itself does not say which number goes with which document, so the reverse pairing is just as possible.

steps.title: More ties means more witnesses
steps.stepSummary: The tied document already has extra requirements, the ties, so it makes sense that it also gets the extra witness.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since it has more in its ties, it has more in its witnesses.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge with a סברא. The document that is already more demanding should be the one that gets more witnesses.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A מקושר needs folding, sewing, and signing between the folds, so it is the more complicated document. The extra requirement, three witnesses, fits with the document that already has extra requirements. That is why the pairing cannot be reversed.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Since' or 'because.' Introduces a reason
'It has more,' it has extra requirements
Its ties, the knots and folds of the tied document

phrases.english: Since it has more in its ties,
it has more in its witnesses.

steps.whatToRemember: From the פסוק in ירמיהו 32:44: a פשוט has two עדים and a מקושר has three. The tied document gets more witnesses because it already has more ties.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 2.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The numbers could be paired either way, so a פשוט might need three witnesses.
steps.terutzMaskana: The more demanding document, the מקושר, takes the larger number of witnesses.

steps.title: רפרם's source: a different verse in ירמיהו
steps.stepSummary: רפרם learns the two kinds of documents from ירמיהו 32:11. The 'deed of purchase' is a פשוט, 'the sealed one' is a מקושר, and 'the open one' is the plain part inside a tied document.
steps.simpleTranslation: רפרם said: we learn it from here: 'So I took the deed of the purchase, the sealed one, the terms and conditions, and the open one.' 'The deed of the purchase' is a plain document. 'The sealed one' is a tied document. 'And the open one' is the plain part of a tied document.
steps.whatsHappening: A new אמורא, רפרם, brings a different פסוק as the source for the two kinds of documents. He explains each phrase of the פסוק one at a time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a second way to find the source, separate from רבי חנינא's פסוק. The new point is 'the open one': even a tied document has a plain, unfolded section. רפרם reads that phrase as referring to it.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא who brings a different source
'From here.' Introduces a new source
The deed of purchase
'The open one,' the part that is not folded

phrases.english: Rafram said: from here:
"So I took the deed of the purchase,
that which was sealed, the terms and conditions,
and that which was open";
"So I took the deed of the purchase" — this is an ordinary document.
"That which was sealed" — this is a tied document.
"And that which was open" —
this is the ordinary part within a tied document.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different פסוק as the source for the same idea as step 1.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ירמיהו 32:11 hints to the פשוט, the מקושר, and the open part inside a מקושר.

steps.title: The differences between the two documents
steps.stepSummary: 'The terms and conditions' are the rules that tell the two documents apart. A פשוט has two עדים who sign on the front. A מקושר has three עדים who sign on the back.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'The terms and conditions' are the things that separate a plain document from a tied document. How so? This one has two witnesses, and that one has three witnesses. This one has its witnesses inside it, and that one has its witnesses on its back.
steps.whatsHappening: רפרם finishes explaining his פסוק. The words 'the terms and conditions' list the practical differences between the two kinds of documents.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two differences are given. First, the number of witnesses: two for a פשוט and three for a מקושר. Second, where they sign: on the inside, on the writing side, for a פשוט, and on the back for a מקושר. So רפרם's פסוק gives both the number of witnesses and where they sign.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The terms and conditions,' read here as the rules that separate the two documents
Inside it, on the written front side
On its back

phrases.english: "The terms and conditions" —
these are the matters that are between an ordinary document and a tied one.
How so?
This one, its witnesses are two,
phrases.notes: 'This one' is the plain document, and 'that one' in the next lines is the tied document.

phrases.english: and that one, its witnesses are three;
this one, its witnesses are inside it,
and that one, its witnesses are on its back.

steps.whatToRemember: פשוט: two עדים, who sign on the front. מקושר: three עדים, who sign on the back. רפרם learns both differences from ירמיהו 32:11.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up 'this one' and 'that one.' 'This one' is always the פשוט, and 'that one' is always the מקושר.
steps.triggerLanguage: ״הַמִּצְוָה וְהַחֻקִּים״ – אֵלּוּ דְּבָרִים שֶׁבֵּין פָּשׁוּט לִמְקוּשָּׁר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes explaining רפרם's פסוק from step 4.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A פשוט has two witnesses who sign on the front. A מקושר has three witnesses who sign on the back.

steps.title: Challenge to רפרם: Maybe Reverse the Witnesses
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רפרם's reading and suggests the pairing could be flipped: three עדים for a פשוט and two for a מקושר.
steps.simpleTranslation: But I can reverse it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on רפרם's source from step 5. Maybe the plain document needs three witnesses and the tied one needs two.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רפרם showed that there are two kinds of documents, but the verse does not say which one gets two עדים and which gets three. So the גמרא asks what stops us from flipping the pairing. This is the same challenge it raised in step 2 against the first source.

keyTerms.meaning: I will reverse it. The גמרא suggests flipping the proposed pairing.

phrases.english: But I can reverse it!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the witness pairing in רפרם's derivation
steps.kashyaTarget: Which document gets two עדים and which gets three, in רפרם's reading
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The verse shows two kinds of documents but does not say which one gets more witnesses, so the pairing could be flipped.

steps.title: The Tied Document Gets More of Everything
steps.stepSummary: Because the מקושר already has extra requirements, the ties, it makes sense that it also gets the extra witness.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since it has more with its ties, it has more with its witnesses.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge with the same logic as step 3. The tied document is already the more demanding one, so it gets three witnesses.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A מקושר takes extra work because it has to be folded and tied. It is logical that the more demanding document also has the bigger witness requirement. So the pairing cannot be reversed.

keyTerms.meaning: Since; because of
It was given more; it has extra requirements
The ties or knots of a tied document

phrases.english: Since it was given more with its ties,
it is given more with its witnesses.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the 'reverse it' challenge
steps.terutzResolutionType: Logical consistency: the more demanding document gets the bigger requirement
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The pairing of witnesses to documents could go either way.
steps.terutzMaskana: The מקושר, which already needs ties, also gets the extra witness.

steps.title: רמי בר יחזקאל: A New Source from 'Two or Three Witnesses'
steps.stepSummary: רמי בר יחזקאל learns from דברים 19:15 that two עדים go with a פשוט and three go with a מקושר.
steps.simpleTranslation: רמי בר יחזקאל said, from here: 'By two witnesses or by three witnesses a matter shall stand.' If testimony stands with two, why did the verse spell out three? To tell you: two for a plain document, three for a tied one.
steps.whatsHappening: A new אמורא gives a different source for the two kinds of documents. He uses the Torah's rule about witnesses.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If two עדים are already enough, mentioning three looks unnecessary. רמי בר יחזקאל says the extra mention points to a second case: one kind of document needs two and another needs three. He matches two to a פשוט and three to a מקושר.

keyTerms.meaning: Spelled out; specified
A matter shall stand, meaning it is legally established
Testimony

phrases.english: Rami bar Yechezkel said: from here:
"By the mouth of two witnesses
or by the mouth of three witnesses
shall a matter stand"
If their testimony stands with two,
why did it spell out for you three?
To tell you:
two for a plain document, three for a tied one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a third source for the same idea
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The extra mention of three עדים teaches that a מקושר needs three and a פשוט needs two.

steps.title: Challenge to רמי בר יחזקאל: Maybe Reverse It
steps.stepSummary: The same challenge comes back: maybe three עדים go with the פשוט and two with the מקושר.
steps.simpleTranslation: But I can reverse it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רמי בר יחזקאל the same way it challenged the earlier sources. The text repeats the same words.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse says 'two or three', but it does not say which number belongs to which document. So the pairing could be flipped here too.

keyTerms.meaning: A plain, open document with the witnesses signing on the front
A tied document that is folded and tied, with the witnesses signing on the back

phrases.english: But I can reverse it!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the pairing in רמי בר יחזקאל's derivation
steps.kashyaTarget: The match of two עדים to a פשוט and three to a מקושר
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The verse gives two numbers without saying which document each one belongs to.

steps.title: Same Answer: The Tied Document Gets More
steps.stepSummary: The מקושר already has ties, so it also gets the extra witness.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since it has more with its ties, it has more with its witnesses.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the same answer as before. The more demanding document gets three witnesses.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The logic does not depend on which verse is the source. Whatever the source, the document with extra requirements gets the extra witness.

keyTerms.meaning: Witnesses
Three

phrases.english: Since it was given more with its ties,
it is given more with its witnesses.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the 'reverse it' challenge
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The numbers could be matched either way.
steps.terutzMaskana: Three עדים go with the מקושר because it already has extra requirements.

steps.title: Do These Verses Really Teach About Documents?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether these verses really come to teach about two kinds of documents, since each one seems to have its own purpose.
steps.simpleTranslation: Do these verses really come for this? Each one comes for its own matter!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now questions all the sources above at once. It says each verse is needed for something else.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Up to now, the challenges only asked which document gets which number. Now the גמרא questions whether these verses teach about documents at all. If each verse already has another job, it cannot serve as a source here.

keyTerms.meaning: Do these really come for this purpose?
Each and every one
For its own matter

phrases.english: And do these come for this purpose?
phrases.notes: 'These' means all the verses brought above as sources for the two kinds of documents.

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל חַד וְחַד לְמִילְּתֵיהּ הוּא דַּאֲתָא –
phrases.english: Each and every one comes for its own matter!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָנֵי לְהָכִי הוּא דְּאָתוּ? כׇּל חַד וְחַד לְמִילְּתֵיהּ הוּא דַּאֲתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks every source given so far
steps.kashyaTarget: All three derivations of the two kinds of documents
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A verse that is already used for a different lesson cannot also be the source for this law.

steps.title: A ברייתא Shows Each Verse's Own Purpose
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא explains each verse differently: the first is good advice, the second just tells what happened, and the third compares three witnesses to two.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught: 'They shall buy fields with money and write it in a book and seal it' teaches good advice. 'And I took the deed of purchase' is how the event happened. 'By two witnesses or by three witnesses' compares three to two, as in the argument of רבי עקיבא and the רבנן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up its challenge with a ברייתא. The ברייתא gives each verse a different job that has nothing to do with two kinds of documents.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse from ירמיהו about writing and sealing is only advice to keep good records. The verse about the deed of purchase only describes what ירמיהו did. The verse about two or three witnesses teaches that three עדים are treated like two. That leaves no verse free to teach about a פשוט and a מקושר.

keyTerms.meaning: As it was taught in a ברייתא
Good advice, not a binding law
It teaches us
Comparing two things so they share the same law
A dispute

steps.whatToRemember: The גמרא now challenges whether the verses teach about two kinds of documents at all, since a ברייתא gives each verse a different purpose.
steps.confusionAlert: This is not saying that a פשוט and a מקושר don't exist. It only questions whether these verses are the source for them.

phrases.english: For that which was taught:
"They shall buy fields with money,
and write it in a book and seal it"
phrases.notes: ירמיהו 32:44. This is the verse used in step 1.

phrases.english: teaches us good advice.
"And I took the deed of purchase"
phrases.notes: ירמיהו 32:11, the verse רפרם used in step 4.

phrases.english: this is how the event happened.
"By the mouth of two witnesses
or by the mouth of three witnesses"
to compare three to two,
as in the dispute of Rabbi Akiva and the Rabbis!
phrases.notes: Their argument about how three witnesses are like two is discussed in מסכת מכות.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the challenge in step 11 with a ברייתא
steps.raayaObject: The claim that each verse has its own purpose
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא that explains each of the three verses differently

steps.title: The tied document is rabbinic, and the verses are only a hint
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that the מקושר comes from חכמים, and the פסוקים quoted earlier are only an אסמכתא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the tied document is from חכמים, and the verses are just a support.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא showed that each פסוק has its own meaning. So the גמרא gives up on finding a Torah source and says the מקושר is a rabbinic rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 1–10 tried to learn the מקושר and its three עדים from three פסוקים: those of רבי חנינא, רפרם and רמי בר יחזקאל. Steps 11–12 showed that those פסוקים teach other things. So the גמרא now says the פסוקים are only a hint for a rule that חכמים made.

keyTerms.meaning: a tied document, folded and stitched, with witnesses on the folds
from the Rabbis, not from the Torah
just a support; a פסוק used as a hint, not as the real source
the verses

steps.whatToRemember: The מקושר is a rabbinic enactment. The פסוקים quoted for it are only a hint.
steps.confusionAlert: An אסמכתא does not mean the פסוק teaches the law. The law comes from חכמים, and the פסוק is only attached as a reminder.
steps.whyThisMatters: This closes the whole search for a source and opens the question of why חכמים made this rule.

phrases.english: Rather, the tied document is from the Rabbis,
and the verses are merely a support.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to the ברייתא in step 12 by moving the מקושר from Torah law to rabbinic law.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The מקושר is מדרבנן, and the פסוקים are only an אסמכתא.

steps.title: Why did the Rabbis create the tied document?
steps.stepSummary: Now that the מקושר is rabbinic, the גמרא asks what reason led חכמים to make it.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what is the reason חכמים instituted the tied document?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why חכמים made this rule. It is setting up the next step, which gives the answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the Torah does not require a מקושר, then חכמים must have had a practical reason for it. This question looks for that reason.

keyTerms.meaning: what is the reason?
they enacted

phrases.english: And what is the reason the Rabbis instituted the tied document?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows from step 13: since the rule is rabbinic, the גמרא asks for its reason.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The practical reason for the rabbinic enactment of the מקושר.

steps.title: Hot-tempered priests needed time to calm down
steps.stepSummary: In a town full of hot-tempered כהנים who divorced their wives quickly, חכמים made the slow, tied גט so they would have time to cool off.
steps.simpleTranslation: There was a place of כהנים who were very quick-tempered and would divorce their wives. חכמים made an enactment so that in the meantime they would calm down.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question. Writing and tying a מקושר takes a long time, and that delay gave angry husbands a chance to change their minds.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A כהן may not remarry his own ex-wife, so a hasty divorce could never be undone. Making the גט slow to prepare protected these marriages. The rule began as a way to slow things down, not as a way to make the document more valid.

keyTerms.meaning: priests
they were strict and quick to anger
an enactment of the Rabbis
in the meantime
their mind settles; they calm down

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that a technical rule about documents was really made to protect families.

phrases.english: There was a place of priests,
and they were very quick-tempered,
and they would divorce their wives;
phrases.notes: A כהן can't remarry his ex-wife, so a hasty divorce couldn't be fixed later.

phrases.english: so the Rabbis made an enactment,
so that in the meantime they would calm down.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 14.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The מקושר was made to slow down hasty divorces by כהנים, giving them time to reconsider.

steps.title: That explains a גט, but why other documents?
steps.stepSummary: The reason works for a גט, but the גמרא asks why ordinary שטרות can also be written as a מקושר.
steps.simpleTranslation: This works well for bills of divorce. What can be said about other documents?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the reason it just gave. Divorce has nothing to do with loan or sale documents, so why do those come in tied form too?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reason in step 15 applies only to divorce. Yet the מקושר is also used for ordinary documents, and the reason does not seem to cover them.

keyTerms.meaning: this works out well for
bills of divorce
documents, such as loans and sales

phrases.english: This works well for bills of divorce;
what can be said about documents?

steps.triggerLanguage: הָתִינַח גִּיטִּין, שְׁטָרוֹת מַאי אִיכָּא לְמֵימַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges how far the reason given in step 15 reaches.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reason given for the מקושר in step 15
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The reason applies only to divorce, but the מקושר is used for all documents.

steps.title: Treat all documents the same
steps.stepSummary: חכמים applied the מקושר to all שטרות so that people would not treat a גט differently from other documents.
steps.simpleTranslation: So that you should not differentiate between bills of divorce and documents.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that חכמים kept one system for all documents. They did not want a separate rule only for a גט.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The main reason was about divorce. To keep things simple and uniform, חכמים extended the same format to every kind of שטר.

keyTerms.meaning: so that you should not make a difference

steps.whatToRemember: The מקושר was made for a גט, to slow down hasty divorces, and then extended to all שטרות so that they would all follow one rule.

phrases.english: So that you should not differentiate
between bills of divorce and documents.

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּדֵי שֶׁלֹּא תְּחַלֵּק בֵּין גִּיטִּין לִשְׁטָרוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 16.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Extension of the enactment for the sake of uniformity
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The reason fits only a גט, so other documents should not be tied.
steps.terutzMaskana: חכמים extended the rule to all documents so that גיטין and שטרות would not be treated differently.

steps.title: Where do the witnesses sign on a tied document?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens a new topic: where exactly the עדים sign on a מקושר.
steps.simpleTranslation: Where do the witnesses sign?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new practical question about the layout of a מקושר. It is setting up the two opinions that come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A מקושר has folds and ties, so it is not obvious where the signatures should go. The next two steps give two different answers.

keyTerms.meaning: where?
the witnesses sign

phrases.english: Where do the witnesses sign?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new practical topic about the מקושר.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The place on a מקושר where the עדים sign.

steps.title: רב הונא: between the ties
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא says the עדים sign between each tie of the document.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא says: between one tie and the next.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא answers that each signature goes in the space between the tied folds.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In רב הונא's view, the signatures go on the folded and tied parts themselves, in the gaps between the ties.

keyTerms.meaning: an אמורא
a tie or knot on the folded document

phrases.english: Rav Huna says:
between one tie and the next.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב הוּנָא אָמַר: בֵּין קֶשֶׁר לְקֶשֶׁר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the first answer to step 18.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The עדים sign between the ties.

steps.title: רב ירמיה בר אבא: on the back, opposite the writing
steps.stepSummary: רב ירמיה בר אבא says the עדים sign on the back of the document, directly opposite the writing, on the outside.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב ירמיה בר אבא says: on the back of the writing, opposite the writing, on the outside.
steps.whatsHappening: A second אמורא gives a different answer: the signatures go on the reverse side, lined up with the text.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב ירמיה בר אבא disagrees with רב הונא. He places the signatures on the outside back of the document, exactly opposite the written text, and not between the ties.

keyTerms.meaning: an אמורא
on the back of the writing
opposite the writing
on the outside

phrases.english: And Rav Yirmeya bar Abba says:
on the back of the writing,
and opposite the writing, on the outside.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַב יִרְמְיָה בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר: אֲחוֹרֵי הַכְּתָב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with רב הונא's answer in step 19.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The עדים sign on the back, opposite the writing, on the outside.

steps.title: רמי בר חמא brings a story with רבי about a tied document
steps.stepSummary: רמי בר חמא assumes רב הונא means the עדים sign between the ties on the inside. He then brings a story: רבי said a מקושר had no date, until his son showed him the date was hidden in the folds.
steps.simpleTranslation: רמי בר חמא said to רב חסדא: According to רב הונא, who says the witnesses sign between each tie, we assume he means between the ties on the inside. But there was a tied document that came before רבי, and רבי said, 'There is no date on this!' His son רבי שמעון said to him, 'Maybe the date is hidden between its ties?' רבי opened it and saw that it was.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a challenge to רב הונא. First it explains how it understands his view, and then it tells a story that will be used against that view in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רמי בר חמא reads 'between each tie' as meaning inside the folds, where the writing is. The story shows that when a מקושר is folded closed, whatever is inside the folds cannot be seen. רבי missed the date because it was hidden in a fold.

keyTerms.meaning: A tie or knot. Each fold of a מקושר is tied shut.
On the inside
We would have thought, or our first assumption is
The date written in a document
Hidden or swallowed up, here meaning tucked inside a fold

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָמֵי בַּר חָמָא לְרַב חִסְדָּא:
phrases.english: Rami bar Ḥama said to Rav Ḥisda:

phrases.aramaic: לְרַב הוּנָא דְּאָמַר בֵּין קֶשֶׁר לְקֶשֶׁר –
phrases.english: According to Rav Huna, who says the witnesses sign between each tie,

phrases.aramaic: קָא סָלְקָא דַּעְתִּין בֵּין קֶשֶׁר לְקֶשֶׁר מִגַּוַּאי –
phrases.english: we assume he means between each tie on the inside
phrases.notes: 'Inside' means within the folds, on the side with the writing.

phrases.aramaic: וְהָא הָהוּא מְקוּשָּׁר דַּאֲתָא לְקַמֵּיהּ דְּרַבִּי,
phrases.english: But there was a certain tied document that came before Rabbi,
phrases.notes: 'רבי' on its own means רבי יהודה הנשיא.

phrases.english: and Rabbi said: There is no date on this!

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בְּרַבִּי לְרַבִּי:
phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon, son of Rabbi, said to Rabbi:
Perhaps it is hidden between its ties?
He opened it and saw it.
phrases.notes: רבי untied the folds and found that the date really was inside.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא הָהוּא מְקוּשָּׁר דַּאֲתָא לְקַמֵּיהּ דְּרַבִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes רב הונא's view from step 19, gives it a reading ('inside'), and brings a story that will be used to test that reading.
steps.raayaObject: That anything written inside the folds of a closed מקושר cannot be seen. Step 22 uses this against the 'inside' reading of רב הונא.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The story of the מקושר that came before רבי, whose date was hidden inside the folds

steps.title: רבי should have said the witnesses were missing too
steps.stepSummary: If the עדים signed inside the folds, רבי would also have seen no signatures. So he should have said 'there is no date and there are no witnesses.'
steps.simpleTranslation: And if it is so that the witnesses sign inside, רבי should have said: 'There is no date on this and there are no witnesses on this!'
steps.whatsHappening: Here the story is turned into an attack. Since רבי complained only about the date, the signatures must have been visible, so they could not have been inside the folds.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A document with no visible signatures is a far bigger problem than a missing date. רבי's silence about witnesses shows they were visible from the outside. That contradicts the 'inside' reading of רב הונא.

keyTerms.meaning: And if it were so (if your claim were true)
He should have said, or it should have been necessary for him to say

phrases.english: And if it is so,
phrases.notes: Meaning: if the witnesses really signed inside the folds.

phrases.english: 'There is no date on this, and there are no witnesses on this'
he should have said!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the conclusion from the story in step 21 and uses it against the 'inside' reading of רב הונא.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's view, read as 'the עדים sign between the ties on the inside'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Signatures inside the folds would be hidden like the date. רבי mentioned only the date, so the signatures must have been visible.

steps.title: רב חסדא: רב הונא meant the outside
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא rejects the assumption. רב הונא meant the עדים sign between the ties on the outside, where they can be seen even when the document is closed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said to him: Do you think he meant between the ties on the inside? No, he meant between the ties on the outside.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא answers the challenge. He keeps רב הונא's rule but explains it differently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge only worked against the 'inside' reading. If the signatures are on the outside between the ties, they stay visible when the document is folded. That fits the story perfectly: רבי saw the witnesses but not the date.

keyTerms.meaning: Do you think?
On the outside

phrases.english: He said to him: Do you think
phrases.notes: רב חסדא is answering רמי בר חמא.

phrases.english: between each tie on the inside?
No, between each tie on the outside.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 22 by changing the reading of רב הונא's view.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpretation of the statement being attacked
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב הונא meant the עדים sign between the ties on the inside, where they would be hidden.
steps.terutzMaskana: רב הונא meant the עדים sign between the ties on the outside, where they are visible, so the story with רבי fits.
steps.whatToRemember: According to רב הונא as explained by רב חסדא, the עדים on a מקושר sign between the ties on the outside.

steps.title: Worry that someone could add forged text
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא worries that since the signatures are between the ties and not right after the writing, someone could add whatever he wants to the open part of the document, and the signatures would already be there.
steps.simpleTranslation: But let us worry that perhaps he forged it and wrote whatever he wanted, and the witnesses are already signed!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a new problem with רב הונא's method: it could allow forgery.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In a regular document the עדים sign right after the last line, so nothing can be added. In a מקושר signed between the ties, part of the document is open and unfolded, away from the signatures. Someone could write extra terms there, and it would look as if the עדים had signed on them.

keyTerms.meaning: And let us worry about it
He forged
Witnesses (Aramaic for עדים)

phrases.english: But let us worry that perhaps he forged
phrases.notes: 'He' is the person holding the document, who could gain by adding terms.

phrases.english: and wrote whatever he wanted,
and the witnesses are signed!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts the 'outside, between the ties' explanation from step 23 and raises a practical problem with it.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's method of signing between the ties
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the signatures are not placed right after the end of the text, there is open space where forged text could be added above signatures that are already there.

steps.title: The document ends with ״שריר וקיים״
steps.stepSummary: The answer is that the document has the words ״שריר וקיים״ ('confirmed and established') written at the end of the text. Anything written after that is ignored, so forgery does not help.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is written in it: 'Confirmed and established.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the forgery worry. The document closes with a fixed phrase that marks where the real text ends.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ״שריר וקיים״ works like a seal at the end of the text. Any words written after it are not part of the document. So even if someone adds text in the open space, it has no legal force.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Confirmed and established', the closing phrase that marks the end of a document's text
Where it is written in it

phrases.english: Where it is written in it: 'Confirmed and established.'
phrases.notes: Since this phrase marks the end of the text, anything added after it doesn't count.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the forgery worry of step 24.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Practical safeguard that removes the concern
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Signing between the ties leaves room for someone to add forged text above the signatures.
steps.terutzMaskana: The phrase ״שריר וקיים״ closes the text, so anything written after it is ignored.
steps.whatToRemember: The forgery worry about a מקושר is solved by ״שריר וקיים״: it marks the end of the document, and anything written after it does not count.
steps.whyThisMatters: ״שריר וקיים״ became a standard closing phrase in שטרות. It shows how חכמים built safeguards into the wording of documents to stop forgery.

steps.title: What if the forger writes a second 'confirmed and established'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the ״שריר וקיים״ answer. A forger could add his own text and then write another ״שריר וקיים״ after it.
steps.simpleTranslation: But let us worry that maybe he wrote whatever he wanted and then wrote another ״שריר וקיים״!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the last answer. It suggests the forger could get around ״שריר וקיים״ by adding text and then writing a new ״שריר וקיים״ after it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 25 the protection was that anything written after ״שריר וקיים״ is ignored. But if the forger adds his text and then writes a fresh ״שריר וקיים״ at the end, his added text now looks like it comes before the closing words. So the old protection seems to fail.

keyTerms.meaning: Let us worry / be concerned
Perhaps, maybe
Whatever he wants
And then, afterward
Another one

phrases.english: But let us be concerned that perhaps he wrote whatever he wanted,
phrases.notes: "He" is the person holding the document, who wants to add things to it.

phrases.english: and then wrote another "confirmed and established"!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of Step 25 that ״שריר וקיים״ blocks additions.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that ״שריר וקיים״ protects the document from added text.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A forger can add text and then write a second ״שריר וקיים״, making his additions look like part of the real document.

steps.title: A document only has one 'confirmed and established'
steps.stepSummary: The answer: we only write ״שריר וקיים״ once. A second one shows that everything after the first was added, so it is ignored.
steps.simpleTranslation: We write one ״שריר וקיים״; we do not write two ״שריר וקיים״.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that a proper document has only one ״שריר וקיים״. So a second one does not help the forger.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the standard practice is to write it only once, the first ״שריר וקיים״ is always the real end of the document. Whatever comes after it, even if a second ״שריר וקיים״ follows, is treated as extra and ignored.

keyTerms.meaning: One
Two
We write

phrases.english: We write one "confirmed and established";
we do not write two "confirmed and established."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 26.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Establishes a fixed writing practice that exposes the forgery.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A second ״שריר וקיים״ could make the forger's added text look valid.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only one ״שריר וקיים״ is ever written, so the first one marks the end and anything after it is ignored.

steps.title: What if the forger erases the original 'confirmed and established'?
steps.stepSummary: A new challenge: the forger could erase the real ״שריר וקיים״, write his own text there, and then write ״שריר וקיים״ after it, so there is still only one.
steps.simpleTranslation: But let us worry that maybe he erased the ״שריר וקיים״, wrote whatever he wanted, and then wrote ״שריר וקיים״!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries a smarter forgery. Instead of writing a second ״שריר וקיים״, the forger erases the first one, so the document still ends up with only one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer in Step 27 only works if there are two ״שריר וקיים״ in the document. If the forger erases the original and writes one new one after his added text, there is only one, and the rule from Step 27 does not catch him.

keyTerms.meaning: He erases

phrases.aramaic: וְלֵיחוּשׁ דִּלְמָא מָחֵיק לֵיהּ לְ״שָׁרִיר וְקַיָּים״,
phrases.english: But let us be concerned that perhaps he erased the "confirmed and established,"
and wrote whatever he wanted,
and then wrote "confirmed and established"!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gets around the answer of Step 27 by imagining a forger who ends up with only one ״שריר וקיים״.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the 'only one ״שריר וקיים״' rule prevents forgery.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the original is erased and replaced after the added text, there is still only one ״שריר וקיים״, so the forgery would not be noticed.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן's rule about corrections between the lines
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא starts to answer by quoting רבי יוחנן: a word added between the lines is valid only if it is confirmed. The answer continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: But רבי יוחנן said: a document with a word hung between the lines, if it is confirmed, is valid...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins its answer by bringing a rule from רבי יוחנן about changes in a document. This is only the start of the quote; the rest of the answer comes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן teaches that a correction written between the lines (תלויה) is valid only if it is confirmed (מקויימת). The idea is that changes to a document are not simply trusted on their own. The גמרא will use this to show why erasing ״שריר וקיים״ does not help the forger.

keyTerms.meaning: But hasn't he said? (bringing a known teaching as an answer)
Literally 'hanging': a word added between the lines
Confirmed (the correction is verified in the document)
Valid

steps.confusionAlert: This step stops in the middle of רבי יוחנן's teaching. Do not think the answer is finished here; it continues on the next amud.

phrases.english: But didn't Rabbi Yochanan say:
A suspended correction: if it is confirmed, it is valid,
phrases.notes: A "suspended" correction is a word squeezed in above the line. "Confirmed" means the document itself notes that the correction is real.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins answering the challenge of Step 28.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Brings an existing rule (רבי יוחנן) about changes in documents to answer the forgery worry.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A forger could erase ״שריר וקיים״ and replace it without anyone noticing.
steps.terutzMaskana: Changes to a document are valid only when confirmed; the full application continues on the next amud.
